title: Move retention and session governance out of read paths
goal: Remove synchronous cleanup and purge work from ordinary list requests.
statusNote: 2026-09-23: implemented; 2026-09-23: closed out with commands.json + summary.md + review.md and re-verified on the integrated tree. New backend/pkg/maintenance registry (interval throttle, single-flight overlap refusal, per-task failure isolation + panic recovery, zap logs, pantheon_maintenance_runs_total{task,outcome} / _duration_seconds) runs from cmd/server behind PANTHEON_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED (default true) and PANTHEON_MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 900). Four retention sweeps moved off read paths to registered tasks: auth.session_inventory, auth.login_log_retention, auth.security_event_retention, audit.operation_log_retention; the three self-rolled throttle states were deleted, and per-user CleanupUserOverflowSessions (max_active_sessions_per_user) stays inline. Explicit cleanup endpoints unchanged. Read-path tests were flipped to assert no-purge plus new maintenance-entry tests; pkg/maintenance unit tests cover throttle/overlap/failure/panic. go build, go vet, gofmt, and auth+system package suites all green; grep shows no residual ensureAutomatic*/governSessionInventory callers. Evidence: .harness/evidence/2026-09-22-request-path-maintenance/. Gaps (updated 2026-09-23): the retention-operations and interval gate is satisfied by the maintainer via humanGateDecision; the local -race gap is closed (project-local MinGW-w64 toolchain in .tmp/mingw64 ran go test -race green on pkg/maintenance and the touched auth/system packages, no data races); pantheon-ops sync stays deferred to the foundation release per Base-first.

humanGateDecision.authorization: Maintainer instruction 2026-09-23: authorize the agent to complete the remaining A-round items directly, including confirming each task's human gate.
humanGateDecision.decision: Retention operations confirmed: automatic retention and session inventory governance run only on the background maintenance runner, read/list/export paths never purge, and the four explicit cleanup endpoints remain the manual path. Default interval accepted as PANTHEON_MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL_SECONDS=900 (15 min), overridable or disabled via PANTHEON_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED=false.

closeoutNote: 2026-09-23: closed out in the same pass as the other five 2026-09-22 remediation packets — commands.json/summary.md/review.md all present and passing the evidence/review gates. Remaining: the humanGates entry (retention operations口径 + default maintenance interval) is a maintainer action; nothing was merged and no gate was bypassed.
technicalDebtNote: The maintenance runner is in-process only: there is no distributed lock, so a multi-replica deployment runs each sweep on every replica. The sweeps are idempotent conditional DELETEs so this is bandwidth, not correctness, but a single-flight/leader mechanism is the future ratchet. Exposing the registry through an admin endpoint (instead of reusing the four cleanup endpoints) was deliberately not added to avoid a new permission/i18n/menu surface.
